# Marketplace implementation plan

**Goal:** Publish template and author pages from the shared catalog and provide a tested manual contribution path followed by guided submission.

**Architecture:** The website consumes JSON generated by the catalog's Python reader. CI parses every bundled package and validates the catalog/author graph. A submission skill later guides the same manual process and produces exact-commit test information.

**Spec:** [Design](../design.md), [metadata](../metadata.md), [website](../specs/website-marketplace/spec.md), [submission](../specs/marketplace-submission/spec.md).

**Status:** Approved delivery direction; implementation not started. Mahmoud will supply marketplace website UI designs separately. This plan defines data and behavior, not a substitute visual design.

## Dependencies

- Data generation and pages depend on the catalog reader and metadata contract from the catalog plan.
- Marketplace visual implementation additionally requires the supplied UI designs.
- Website and CI do not depend on the export skill, validation HTTP endpoint or GitHub loader. CI can call the current local parser.
- Guided submission follows the tested manual contribution path. Exact-head testing uses the commit-pinned GitHub loader when delivered.

## File responsibilities

- `web/website/src/components/TemplateExplorer.tsx`: current marketplace entry component; inspect before replacing it.
- `web/website/src/pages/`: add routes using the existing Astro conventions and supplied designs.
- `web/website/package.json`: explicit generated-data build prerequisite.
- `api/oss/src/resources/agent_templates/`: catalog, author registry and package directories.
- `api/oss/src/core/agent_templates/parser.py`: one package parser, shared with runtime.
- Proposed `api/oss/src/resources/agent_templates/scripts/validate_marketplace.py`: command-line validation entrypoint, not another parser.
- Proposed `.github/workflows/template-catalog-validation.yml`: full validation and immutable-package checks.
- `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py`: inspect product skill registration for submit-template.

Read `web/website/AGENTS.md` and the website's existing component/test conventions before UI work. Proposed `/templates`, `/templates/<key>` and `/templates/authors/<id>` routes must be reconciled with current routes and supplied designs before implementation.

## Task 1: Full validation and manual contributions

- [ ] Write tests for valid catalog/package trees, missing authors, invalid package mappings, unsupported formats and modifications to a published package version.
- [ ] Implement a command that validates all bundled packages and the full catalog/author graph through existing Python code. Do not select only changed packages.
- [ ] Compare package paths/bytes against the base branch to reject overwriting existing published versions. Use a sufficient Git fetch for this comparison; do not require full history for ordinary parsing.
- [ ] Add a PR workflow triggered by package/catalog changes and by changes to the parser, reader or validation entrypoint. Run fork contributions with read-only permissions and no secrets. Never execute package-provided scripts.
- [ ] Prove the check passes valid fixtures and fails deliberately invalid ones. Measure full validation time. Add selective validation only in a later change justified by that measurement.
- [ ] Write the manual contribution guide: add a versioned package folder, add/reuse an author, update the catalog, validate locally and submit a PR. Derive the exact command from the implemented entrypoint.
- [ ] Rehearse it on a scratch branch/fork with appropriate approval for external writes. Request maintainer authorization before marking a workflow check required; this PR does not change repository settings.

## Task 2: Wire generated website data

- [ ] Consume the deterministic JSON generator from the catalog plan. Do not port normalization into TypeScript.
- [ ] Write parity tests for card fields, examples, author membership, selected package versions and derived summaries.
- [ ] Make the build fail with an actionable message for invalid author/package references, rather than emitting broken pages.
- [ ] Run the website build and data tests before visual implementation. This task does not require the import/export feature.

## Task 3: Apply supplied marketplace UI designs

- [ ] Obtain Mahmoud's website designs and map each screen to catalog fields, routes and loading/empty/error behavior. Resolve a missing field or conflict explicitly; do not invent a redesigned marketplace.
- [ ] Implement the index, template detail and author pages using the current website stack and those designs.
- [ ] Write tests for descriptions, author links, image/video rendering and missing-media fallbacks. Derive author membership from catalog references.
- [ ] Add a "Use it for free" button for each template in listings and detail pages, carrying its stable key to the destination app. Reuse the existing authentication/project flow; do not add a website authentication service or self-hosted destination picker.
- [ ] Connect the pending-template consumer to actual package loading. At the checked baseline, `web/oss/src/components/pages/agent-home/hooks/useConsumePendingTemplate.ts` calls `useCreateAgent` with name/seed only, while `useCreateAgent.ts` already accepts a `template` argument for package loading. Recheck current code and connect that path rather than preserve blank-agent seeding.
- [ ] Migrate `web/oss/src/state/url/template.ts` and the pending consumer away from static `AGENT_TEMPLATES` lookup with the catalog migration. Keep a captured key while catalog data loads; distinguish an unresolved lookup from a confirmed unavailable key. Preserve the existing auth capture, pending-selection lifetime and claim safeguards, including the distinction between website auto-creation links and in-app `?new=1` preselection.
- [ ] Test signed-in creation, signup/verification/provider round trips, existing-account sign-in, required project setup, repeated callbacks/refresh, and unavailable keys. Assert the created agent has the selected package configuration, not only its name/prompt. The user must not reselect the template after authentication.
- [ ] Build published pages only from merged catalog entries. Preview builds may show proposed entries; unmerged authors do not require published pages.
- [ ] Run tests/build, check small and large viewports, and capture real page screenshots for design review before merge.

## Task 4: Guided submission

- [ ] After the manual path works, add submit-template guidance through the product's built-in skill mechanism. Start from a validated export or package folder; reuse author records and collect missing listing information.
- [ ] Guide GitHub authentication without collecting credentials in chat. Explain fork/branch steps for a first-time contributor.
- [ ] Run the same validation command used by CI. Obtain approval for the PR title/body before publishing the contribution.
- [ ] Include head repository, full commit SHA and package path. Rehearse loading that exact source through the commit-pinned importer.
- [ ] Test first-time and returning contributors. Fix the skill and manual guide together when a step fails.

## Task 5: Publication rehearsal

- [ ] On a fork rehearsal or first authorized real merge, verify that normal website builds publish pages and the next app release includes the catalog entry without manual registration.
- [ ] Verify an older app missing the key reports unavailable/version information rather than loading another template.
- [ ] Record exact commits and evidence. Do not claim a future production release was verified from a local build.

## Verification

After dependency setup, from `web/`:

```sh
pnpm --filter website test
pnpm --filter website build
```

Run the new Python validation entrypoint plus focused API tests from the catalog plan. Record workflow pass/fail evidence and UI review against the supplied designs. These are implementation acceptance checks, not completed results from this documentation PR.
